title: My Mom Said My Games Cost Me My Friends #shorts

cast.kid: a stick-figure boy with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, messy black hair and a green hoodie
cast.mom: a stick-figure mother with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, a short blonde bob and a red cardigan
cast.teacher: a stick-figure math teacher with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, gray curly hair, square glasses and a blue sweater

lines.text: Mom said my games left me with fewer friends than anyone, so was she right?
lines.image: {kid} alone on a living room floor holding a game controller, looking up worried, a glowing TV behind him

lines.text: Mom scrolled my game's friend list, where every player shows how many friends they have.
lines.image: {mom} alone on a couch scrolling a tablet with a long blank list on the screen, eyebrows raised

lines.text: "Every single friend of yours has more friends than you," she said with a frown.
lines.image: {mom} alone in a living room, frowning, holding a tablet out at arm's length

lines.text: "That's too much gaming, so the console stays off until you make more friends."
lines.image: {mom} alone carrying a game console under one arm toward a hallway closet, stern face

lines.text: I checked, and every one of my friends really did have more friends than me.
lines.image: {kid} alone at a desk in his room staring at a tablet, mouth open in shock

lines.text: I sat on my floor staring at that list, feeling like the loneliest kid alive.
lines.image: {kid} alone sitting on the floor of his room hugging his knees, a tablet beside him, sad, a tear on his cheek

lines.text: Next day my math teacher smiled, "That's the friendship paradox, and it fools even grown-ups."
lines.image: {teacher} alone in a classroom smiling and pointing at a chalkboard covered in simple dot-and-line drawings

lines.text: "A kid with fifty friends is on fifty lists; a quiet kid is on two."
lines.image: {teacher} alone at a chalkboard drawing one big dot with many lines and one small dot with two lines

lines.text: "So popular kids crowd every list, and most of your friends end up more popular."
lines.image: {teacher} alone in a classroom spreading both arms wide, chalkboard of connected dots behind

lines.text: So I had Mom open her own friend page, and Mom never plays games.
lines.image: {kid} alone in a living room holding out a phone toward the viewer, confident grin

lines.text: Almost every friend on her list had more friends than her, and her jaw dropped.
lines.image: {mom} alone on a couch staring at her phone, jaw dropped, eyes wide

lines.text: Games never cost me friends, so the console came back, and now Mom blames math.
lines.image: {kid} alone on the living room floor happily playing a video game, a glowing TV in front of him, warm evening light
